clue.text: Nothing fits with information detectives last gave on killing

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information
nothing is zero, written as the letter O
the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the following word, gave, and nothing more of it

parts.note: the final letter of gave

explanation.surface: Detectives pass on a tip that cracks a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is reshuffled: the information comes first, then nothing, then the detectives and the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Genocide is the deliberate mass slaughter of a people, so killing on a vast scale.

clue.text: French port is rather unsophisticated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French word for left, and port is the left side of a ship
second meaning: socially awkward or clumsy

explanation.surface: A traveller judges some harbour town in France to be a bit backward.
explanation.walkthrough: French port looks like a harbour such as Calais; read it as the French for port, the ship's left side.
explanation.definitionFit: The English adjective borrowed from French describes someone tactless, clumsy and lacking social grace.

clue.text: On retiring, remains a person without influence

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the little word on is read in the backward direction

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round
a dead body is someone's remains

explanation.surface: Once someone steps down from office, what remains is a figure with no clout.
explanation.walkthrough: Remains looks like a verb meaning stays; it is the noun, a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a nobody means they are unimportant, having no status or power.

clue.text: Cash in fancy jewellery

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to dream up or elaborate, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sells off ornate gems and trinkets for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck chains of gold or silver are a common kind of ornament worn as personal adornment.

clue.text: Well-established journalist perching on low chair

indicators.note: in a down clue, perching on puts the journalist beneath what follows, so it is joined at the end

parts.note: a deep voice or note is low
a chair is a seat
short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter balances on a squat armchair, firmly settled in their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-seated prejudices or fears are firmly rooted, long held and hard to remove.

clue.text: Made off without us, feeling tickled

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of made are disarranged
without in its old sense means outside, so the jumbled letters sit around the pronoun

parts.note: the letters of made rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away leaving the group behind, and finds it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: Made off looks like ran away; made is the fodder, off the signal, and without means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tickled in the figurative sense is being entertained and finding something funny.

clue.text: Servant and head gardener upset over tropical tree

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the following word is scrambled

parts.note: a manservant, as in man Friday

indicators.note: head points to the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the opening letter of gardener
the letters of over rearranged

explanation.surface: A butler and a chief gardener get upset about a tree on a hot estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are trees and shrubs of tropical coastal swamps, growing in salty tidal water.

clue.text: Try hard to fix legs holding gardener's basket

indicators.note: to fix something is to rework or arrange it, so the following word is put in a new order
holding means gripping something inside, so the rearranged letters wrap around the basket

parts.note: the letters of legs rearranged
a trug is a shallow wooden basket used by British gardeners

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to mend the feet of a garden basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to make a great effort against difficulty, straining to succeed.

clue.text: Substitute for topsy-turvy exercise in river

indicators.note: in places the exercise inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, which in a down clue turns the exercise end over end

parts.note: a sit-up is a stomach exercise

explanation.surface: A swimmer stands in for someone doing upside-down workouts in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Exercise looks like PE, the usual abbreviation, but here it is a whole sit-up flipped to PUTIS inside the DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise for someone is to act in their place, standing in temporarily as their deputy.

clue.text: Just pay attention to upper-class ideas for a change!

indicators.note: for a change asks that the word before it be altered, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage
nota bene, Latin for note well
the letters of ideas rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to listen to the posh people's views, just this once.
explanation.walkthrough: Just looks like merely; it is the adjective meaning fair. The upper-class letter comes before the note-well abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A just judgement is fair and impartial, showing no favour or prejudice toward either side.

clue.text: Deceive tipsy parent

indicators.note: tipsy means slightly drunk and unsteady, so the following word staggers into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A child fools a mother or father who has had a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to trick someone into a compromising act, a form of deliberately misleading them.

clue.text: Is getting married after wild hen do the height of indulgence?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the party phrase run loose
after puts the married pair of pieces behind the jumbled party letters

parts.note: the letters of hen do rearranged; a hen do is a British bride's pre-wedding party
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A rowdy hen night before the wedding might be the peak of excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure above all, so it is self-indulgence taken to its extreme.

clue.text: Panic newspaper spread about doctor joining hospital

indicators.note: spread about means laid out around something, so the newspaper wraps the rest

parts.note: the Financial Times, a London daily

indicators.note: joining attaches the hospital letter after the doctor word

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A paper's front-page story about a medic at a hospital causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a medic; it is the verb meaning falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock of fear, which is close to a moment of panic.

clue.text: Laying off workers embarrassed humanitarian body — and shocked disheartened charity

indicators.note: shocked means jolted out of place, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
the United Nations
the letters of and rearranged

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, leaving only the outside letters of the following word

parts.note: the first and last letters of charity

explanation.surface: Staff cuts at an aid agency leave a demoralised charity reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: And looks like a mere link word but it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundancy is the British term for dismissal because a job is no longer needed.

clue.text: Bankside residents with broken elevators

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of the machines are reassembled

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the letters of elevators rearranged

explanation.surface: Riverside flat dwellers grumble about lifts that are out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: Bankside suggests a London district; here it is a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Water voles are small rodents that burrow into the banks of rivers and streams, living there.

clue.text: Government ministry united by overdue change

parts.note: the Ministry of Defence
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names
something overdue is late

explanation.surface: A department of state joins forces over a long-delayed reform.
explanation.definitionFit: To modulate is to vary or adjust something, such as the pitch or strength of a voice.

clue.text: Sharp footwear?

parts.note: surface reading: smart, stylish shoes
setter's reading: a high thin heel named after a slender dagger, literally pointed

explanation.walkthrough: Sharp suggests fashionable, but the shoe heel is named after a narrow blade, so it is sharp in the literal sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a thin-bladed dagger and a woman's shoe with a tall, narrow, pointed heel.

clue.text: Sports equipment demonstrated adventurous streak in women's organisation

indicators.note: adventurous suggests roaming freely, so the following word's letters wander into a new order
in places the reworked letters inside the organisation's abbreviation

parts.note: the Women's Institute, a British community group
the letters of streak rearranged

explanation.surface: A members' club of genteel women shows a surprisingly daring side by taking up a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-ski is the long board worn on each foot when towed across a lake behind a boat.

clue.text: Public anger — and love — for America is excessive

indicators.note: for here means standing as, so the country abbreviation follows as the next piece

parts.note: public anger is outrage
love is zero in tennis, written as O
the United States

explanation.surface: A pundit says the nation's fury and affection toward the States are both overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make love seem an aside; it is a piece, the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrageous behaviour or prices go far beyond what is reasonable, being shockingly extreme.

clue.text: Block demand for fine fabric

parts.note: a dam blocks a river
to ask for something firmly is to demand it

explanation.surface: A trader refuses an order for luxury cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich woven cloth, often silk or linen, with a pattern visible on both sides.

clue.text: Half sure woman has something in her eye

indicators.note: half means only part is kept, so two of the four letters of sure are dropped

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut in two
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is fairly certain she has a speck in her eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of sure is kept. Something in her eye sounds like a speck of dust, but it is part of every eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eyeball, so it is literally inside it.

clue.text: Nat has returned to South Africa with a bit of poetry

indicators.note: returned means gone back, so the name with its contraction is read backwards

parts.note: Nat has contracts to Nat's
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A man named Nat comes home to Cape Town carrying a few lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Has must be read as the apostrophe-s of Nat's to supply the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit within a poem, much like a verse.

clue.text: To stay inside weaving rug seems less attractive

indicators.note: weaving means interlacing threads, so the letters of the following word are interlaced afresh
inside puts the verb within the other letters

parts.note: the letters of rug rearranged
to lie low is to stay put

explanation.surface: Keeping a half-woven carpet indoors makes the room look worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglier is the comparative of ugly, so it means plainer or less pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Alongside being a radio presenter, is expert with books

parts.note: a plus DJ, a disc jockey
an ace is an expert
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone moonlights as a DJ while also being skilled at accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Alongside looks like a preposition meaning as well as; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent things lie next to each other, neighbouring and side by side.

clue.text: Painter skips first part — it's complicated

indicators.note: skips first means the opening letter of the following word is passed over and dropped

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

indicators.note: complicated means tangled, so the letters of it's are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A decorator skips the opening section of a job, saying it is too fiddly.
explanation.walkthrough: It's looks like a contraction joining the halves; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of pictures is a kind of creative practitioner of the fine arts.

clue.text: Offensive occupation?

parts.note: surface reading: a distasteful or rude job
setter's reading: a military attack that seizes and holds territory

explanation.walkthrough: Offensive looks like rude and occupation like job; read them as a military assault and taking over land.
explanation.definitionFit: An invasion is an armed incursion into another country, an attack aimed at seizing its territory.

clue.text: It's stimulating to be back in Eric's embrace

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word inside the name
an embrace wraps around, so the name holds the other piece

parts.note: the man's name, holding the other letters

indicators.note: back means going in reverse, so the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Returning to a lover's arms is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic material arouses sexual desire, so it is exciting in a sensual way.

clue.text: Sports meeting for health club at which foreign prince gets first aid

parts.note: a gym is a fitness club
a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the opening letter of aid

explanation.surface: A visiting royal is treated at a fitness centre after a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: First aid looks like emergency treatment; it is just the first letter of aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is a British horse-riding event with races and games, often for children on ponies.
